title: Buying tickets online and at the gate
body: Day tickets are cheaper online than at the gate and can be bought up to the morning of the visit. Each ticket is a QR code in the park app or on a printed page, and one code admits one guest. Children under three enter free but still need a ticket so the park can count heads for evacuation planning. Tickets are dated, so a ticket for Saturday will not scan on Sunday; changing the date is free up to twenty-four hours before the visit and not possible after. Prices vary by season and by day of the week, with weekends and school holidays costing more. The gate sells tickets by card only. Guests who arrive with a ticket bought from a reseller should check it before travelling, because resold codes are often already used and the park cannot honor them. A ticket scanned on the wrong day is turned away with GATE-4107.

title: Season pass rejected at the turnstile
body: A season pass that is scanned three times within ten minutes locks for thirty minutes and returns GATE-4102 on every further attempt, including a correct scan. This usually happens when a family scans one phone for several people, or when a guest leaves and immediately re-enters. The lock clears on its own. Guest Services at the main entrance can clear it at once, and there is no need to buy a day ticket in the meantime. To avoid it, give each member of a group their own pass in the app so that each phone is scanned once. A pass that is rejected with no code at all is a different problem, usually a screen too dim for the scanner to read; turning the brightness up fixes it more often than anything else.

title: What the Fast Fossil pass covers
body: The Fast Fossil pass lets its holder use the short queue at every ride and show in the park except Swamp Safari. Swamp Safari loads jeeps in a fixed order and runs one queue for everybody, so no pass skips it; arriving in the first hour after opening is the best way to keep that wait short. The pass is valid for one day and one guest, and it is tied to that guest's ticket, so it cannot be handed on to another member of the party partway through the day. Each ride can be used with the pass once per hour. Fast Fossil can be added to a ticket at any point before or during the visit, and it cannot be refunded once any ride has been used with it.

title: Refunds, date changes, and weather closures
body: Day tickets can be refunded in full up to forty-eight hours before the date on the ticket, from the booking page. Inside forty-eight hours the date can still be changed until the day before, but the ticket cannot be refunded. On days when the park closes early because of lightning or high winds, every guest who entered that day is offered a rain check voucher, which works as a free ticket for any date in the following twelve months. The voucher appears in the app automatically once the closure is announced; there is nothing to claim. A single ride closing does not count as a park closure and does not earn a voucher. Refunds go back to the card that paid, and take up to ten days to appear.

title: Annual pass suspended after a failed payment
body: Annual passes paid monthly are suspended when a payment fails, and the app shows PASS-3300 against the pass until the balance is cleared. A suspended pass will not scan at the turnstile. The most common cause is a card that was replaced by the bank, often after a fraud alert, while the old number stayed on file. Update the card in the app under Passes, then Payment, and then choose Retry payment; updating the card alone does not retry the charge, and the pass stays suspended until the next scheduled attempt. Once payment succeeds the pass works again within a few minutes. A pass that stays suspended for sixty days is canceled, and the months already paid are not refunded. A suspended pass is also refused at the turnstile with GATE-4109.

title: Group and school bookings
body: Groups of fifteen or more book through the group desk rather than the app, and get a single booking reference covering everyone. Only the organizer named on the booking can change it. When that person leaves the school or company, the group desk can move the booking to a new organizer once the institution confirms the change in writing on its letterhead; this takes up to three working days, so do it well before the trip. School groups receive one free adult place for every ten children. Teachers can download a trip pack with a risk assessment, a map, and a letter describing each ride's safety features, which many schools use for permission slips. Group bookings cannot be split into individual tickets after they are made.

title: Receipts and tax numbers
body: Every purchase produces a receipt in the app and by email. Receipts list each ticket, add-on, and fee as its own line, so a small order can still run to many lines; the total at the bottom is what was charged. A company name or tax number must be entered at checkout, under Billing details, because a receipt cannot be edited once it is issued and the park does not reissue receipts to add them. Groups that need a formal invoice for their accounts should book through the group desk, which issues invoices rather than receipts. Receipts older than two years are removed from the app but can still be requested by email. Food and gift shop purchases are receipted separately at the till.

title: Canceling a season pass
body: A season pass paid in full runs to the end of its season and cannot be canceled partway through for a refund. A season pass paid monthly can be canceled from the app at any time, and the cancellation takes effect at the end of the current month; the pass keeps working until then. Months already paid are not refunded, and no charge is taken after the cancellation date. Guests who cancel can buy a new pass later at whatever the price is then. Passes are personal and cannot be transferred to another person, even within a family. Canceling a pass does not cancel any Fast Fossil add-ons already bought for specific dates; those have to be refunded separately. A canceled pass that is scanned anyway returns GATE-4110.

title: When the monorail makes an emergency stop
body: If the Canopy Monorail detects a fault on the track it brakes and holds every car where it is, and the display inside each car shows RAIL-5510. Every car carries a backup battery that keeps the lights, the fans, and the intercom running for at least two hours, even when the main power is cut. Staff reach a stopped car within thirty minutes and either restart the line or walk guests out along the service gantry. Guests should stay seated and use the intercom for anything urgent, including anyone feeling unwell in the heat; water is stored under the seats in every car. Guests on a stopped monorail are offered a free return visit, which appears in the app within a day.

title: Monorail stations and timetable
body: The Canopy Monorail runs a loop with five stations: Main Gate, T. rex Kingdom, the Hatchery, Raptor Paddock, and the Dino Diner. A car arrives every eight minutes from opening until half an hour before closing. Cars skip the Hatchery station whenever the hatchery is closed for incubation checks, which happens most afternoons, and the display in the car says so before the stop. The loop takes about twenty-five minutes. Doors open on the platform side only; the other side stays locked and cannot be opened from inside. Strollers must be folded before boarding. Wait times at each station are shown in the park app, and they update every two minutes. A station display showing RAIL-5520 means the next car is running late.

title: Swamp Safari jeeps
body: Swamp Safari is a guided jeep tour through the wetland habitat, taking about thirty minutes. The jeeps run on a fixed track, and each seats six with a lap belt at every seat, which must stay fastened for the whole tour. Riders must be at least one meter tall. If a jeep stops on the track, the driver radios the depot and a recovery vehicle tows it clear, usually within twenty minutes; guests stay in their seats while this happens, because the habitat animals are loose on either side. Tours pause during thunderstorms. The jeeps are inspected every morning before opening, and each breakdown is logged and reviewed. Riders who were on a jeep that broke down can ride again without queuing. A jeep that radios RAIL-5530 has left its track and waits for recovery.

title: Swamp Safari photos
body: A camera near the end of Swamp Safari photographs every jeep, and the photos are sent to the app of whoever scanned their ticket to board, usually within an hour. If the booth screen shows PHOTO-2231, the photo was taken but could not be matched to a ticket, which happens when nobody in the jeep scanned in at the loading platform. Those photos are kept for seven days, and staff at the ride exit can find them by the time of the tour and add them to a ticket by hand. Photos in the app are free to download in low resolution; the full-size version is sold as an add-on. Photos taken during a breakdown are not kept.

title: T. rex Kingdom and the feeding show
body: The T. rex is fed in front of a crowd at 2pm every day. After a large meal she usually lies down and stays still for an hour or more, often in full view of the stands, and keepers explain this during the show. It is normal digestion, not illness, and the keepers watch her on camera throughout. Her roar is played through the enclosure speakers every fifteen minutes as part of the show, and the times are posted at the entrance to the kingdom. The stands seat eight hundred, and the front rows get splashed during feeding. Keepers answer questions at the fence for twenty minutes after the show ends.

title: Viewing glass and enclosure barriers
body: Every enclosure window in the park is made of three layers of laminated glass, each strong enough on its own to hold back the animal behind it. The outer layer is the one guests touch, and it is the one that most often chips or cracks, usually from strollers and thrown objects. A crack in the outer layer does not weaken the barrier, but it is still replaced, so please report any crack to the nearest member of staff with its location. Staff close the viewing area until an engineer has checked it. Glass is inspected every night after closing. Guests should not lean on or tap the glass, both for the animals' sake and because tapping is how most chips start.

title: The Raptor Paddock
body: The Raptor Paddock is enclosed by two gates with a holding pen between them, so that the outer gate and the inner gate are never open at once. Guests who see the outer gate open should know that the inner gate is locked whenever that happens, and keepers use the pen to move equipment in and out. Even so, any gate standing open with no keeper in sight should be reported at once to the nearest member of staff. The paddock runs an evening walk on Fridays and Saturdays in summer, bookable as the Paddock Pass, which takes small groups along a raised walkway after dark. Children under eight cannot join the evening walk. Dates for each season are published in the app in spring.

title: How the raptors are kept busy
body: Raptors are clever and get bored, and bored raptors pace and fight. Keepers give them puzzles every day: food hidden in logs, scent trails, and a feeding hatch that the raptors can learn to open from the inside. Watching a raptor open the hatch is part of the design, and the hatch only ever leads into a sealed feeding box, never out of the paddock. The routine changes weekly so the animals do not solve it for good. Keepers log which raptor solves what, and the logs are used to plan the next week. Guests sometimes see keepers apparently ignoring a raptor at work on a puzzle; they are giving it room, not missing it.

title: Pteranodons and the diner patio
body: The pteranodon aviary is open at the top, and a few birds regularly glide over the Dino Diner patio. They are attracted by food held in the air, and they take it in a swoop that can scratch a hand. Eat under the patio umbrellas, keep food low, and do not feed them; hand-fed pteranodons learn to steal and have to be moved to a closed aviary. Staff on the patio carry first aid kits and can clean and dress a scratch on the spot. Anyone scratched should still visit a first aid station, because a keeper records every incident to track which birds are bold. Umbrellas on the patio are closed only in high winds.

title: First aid stations
body: The park has three first aid stations: at the main gate, beside T. rex Kingdom, and next to the Dino Diner. Each is staffed by a nurse from opening until closing, and each is marked on the park map with a green cross. They handle cuts, scratches, heat exhaustion, allergic reactions, and anyone feeling unwell, and they hold spare children's medicine. Every member of staff carries a radio and can call a nurse to wherever a guest is, which is faster than walking to a station for anything serious. For a medical emergency, tell any member of staff, who will call the park ambulance and the local emergency service together. First aid is free.

title: Lost children
body: If a child is lost, tell the nearest member of staff straight away rather than searching alone. Staff announce Code Amber on the park radio, and every exit gate closes to children leaving without an adult while the search runs. Staff will ask for the child's age, clothing, and where they were last seen, so a photo on a phone taken that morning helps a great deal. Most children are found within fifteen minutes, often at a first aid station or with a member of staff. Children who realize they are lost are taught in the park's safety talk to find anyone in a green park shirt. A found child is brought to Guest Services at the main gate, never handed to anyone else.

title: Child ID wristbands
body: Guest Services at the main gate hands out a free Blue Wristband for every child, with space to write a parent's phone number on the inside. Staff who find a child alone check for the band first, and it lets them phone a parent before any announcement is made. The band is waterproof and survives the splash pad and the rides. It cannot be removed without cutting it, and staff will cut it off at the exit if asked. Parents can also add a child's photo to their own app, where staff can see it only after a parent reports the child missing. Bands are available on every day the park is open.

title: Lost and found
body: Items found in the park are logged at Guest Services at the main gate and held for thirty days. Items left on the monorail are held first at the station office where the car was cleaned, and moved to Guest Services at the end of the day. To ask about an item, describe it in the app under Help, then Lost property, with the date and roughly where it was lost; staff match reports against the log each evening and message when there is a likely match. Phones are charged while they wait, in the charging lockers behind Guest Services. Soft toys are washed before they are returned. Items unclaimed after thirty days are donated, except keys and documents, which are destroyed.

title: Dietary needs at the Dino Diner
body: The Dino Diner cooks vegetarian and vegan food on a separate grill from meat, and uses separate fryers for anything marked plant-based on the menu. Every menu item lists its allergens, and staff at the counter can check any dish against the full ingredient list. Kitchen staff change gloves between orders marked for an allergy, and those orders are cooked first and carried out separately. The diner cannot guarantee that nothing has touched nuts, because the bakery that supplies the buns handles them. Gluten-free buns are available on request. Guests with a serious allergy can speak to the duty chef before ordering, and the chef will walk them through the kitchen's procedures.

title: Reporting illness after eating in the park
body: Guests who become ill after eating at any food outlet in the park should report it within seventy-two hours through the app under Help, then Food concern, giving what was eaten, where, and roughly when. Each report goes to the food safety manager, who checks the outlet's records for that day, the temperature logs, and whether anyone else reported the same thing. More than one report about the same outlet on the same day closes it for inspection. Reports are shared with the local health department where the law requires it. Guests are asked whether a doctor was seen, but are not required to give medical details. Receipts help, but a report without one is still investigated.

title: Bringing food and drink into the park
body: Guests may bring their own snacks and sandwiches into the park in soft bags, along with water bottles, which can be refilled for free at fountains throughout the park. Glass containers and hard-sided coolers are not allowed through the gate. Picnic tables are available near the Main Gate station and beside the splash pad, and guests are welcome to eat their own food there. Food brought from outside cannot be eaten inside the Dino Diner. Baby food and formula are always allowed, in any container. Staff at the gate may ask to look inside bags. Please do not feed any park animal, including the ones that seem to be asking for it.

title: Using the park app
body: The park app holds tickets, passes, the map, show times, and live wait times for every ride. Tickets scan straight from the app, and each ticket in a group can be sent to that guest's own phone. The app uses location and keeps the screen bright while showing a ticket, which runs batteries down quickly on a long day; charging lockers are available behind Guest Services and next to the Dino Diner. If the app cannot load at the gate, staff can find any ticket from the name of the person who booked it. The app works without a signal for tickets already downloaded, so open them once before arriving. The app is free.

title: Accessibility and quiet spaces
body: A quiet room behind Guest Services at the main gate is open all day for anyone who needs a break from noise and crowds, with dim lighting and soft seating. Every ride and show is rated for noise, darkness, and sudden movement on the sensory map, which can be picked up at the gate or viewed in the app. The T. rex roar times are posted at the kingdom entrance so they can be avoided. Guests who cannot wait in long queues can register at Guest Services for a return time at each ride instead. Wheelchairs can be borrowed free at the gate. Every monorail station has a lift, and one jeep on Swamp Safari is adapted for a wheelchair.

title: Heat, shade, and water
body: The park gets hot in summer, and most shade is under trees rather than roofs. Queue lines for T. rex Kingdom and Swamp Safari are covered, and both run misting fans along the line on days above thirty degrees. Water fountains are marked on the map, and bottles can be refilled free at any of them. Staff hand out water in long queues on the hottest days. Anyone feeling dizzy or faint should sit in the shade and tell a member of staff, who can call a nurse. Hats and sunscreen are sold at the gift shop by the main gate. On very hot afternoons some keeper talks move indoors, and the app shows where.

title: The hatchery tour
body: The hatchery tour runs at 10am and 1pm and takes groups of up to twenty past the incubators where eggs are kept before hatching. A rope line keeps visitors a meter back from the incubators, and eggs are never handled by guests, because the temperature and humidity inside each incubator are controlled to a fraction of a degree and a touch can chill an egg. If a guide invites guests past the rope, please decline and let Guest Services know; this is against the park's rules for the animals' sake, however kindly meant. The hatchery closes to visitors most afternoons for incubation checks. Tours cannot be booked in advance and fill on a first-come basis at the hatchery door.

title: Splash pad water
body: The splash pad beside the Dino Diner recirculates treated water, and staff test it every hour for chlorine and clarity. If a test fails, or if a guest reports cloudy water or an odd smell, the pad is switched off and emptied, the water replaced, and the pad reopened only after a clean test. Guests should report a smell or cloudy water to any member of staff rather than waiting for the next test. The pad is shallow and designed for children under ten, and swim diapers are required for toddlers. It is closed during thunderstorms and after dark. Towels are sold at the Dino Diner, and changing rooms are next to the pad.

title: Opening hours and seasons
body: The park opens at 9am every day of the year except the last week of January, when it closes for maintenance. Closing time changes with the season: 6pm from November through February, 8pm from March through October, and 10pm on summer Fridays and Saturdays. Last entry is two hours before closing. Some rides open later than the park or close earlier, and the app shows each ride's hours for the day. Early entry at 8am is included with season passes on weekends. School holidays are the busiest days, and weekday mornings in term time are the quietest. The park closes early for lightning or high winds, and closures are announced in the app.
